title: The share of a national news publisher's 26 January 2027 at-risk list of monthly digital subscribers still subscribed on 31 March 2027 because they are sent a half-price retention offer, forecast from last January's randomised test
subdomain: churn propensity and uplift modelling (the effect of a retention offer on a monthly subscription, carried from a randomised test whose deliveries fell at every point of the billing cycle to a list whose bills all fall six days after the send)
prompt_shape: one forecast share to the nearest 5 per cent; last January's offer discounts on February and March 2026 bills and its takers on each plan; this year's list billed for its plans after credits in each month from October 2026 to January 2027 on each plan

distractors.why_relevant: readers' satisfaction and their own stated chance of cancelling in the next three months, which looks like a way to size who on the list would go without the offer
distractors.why_unused: a voluntary sample of both lists' members with stated intentions, no arm and no billing; no figure reads it
distractors.ruled_out_by: its own coverage (a voluntary sample) and the randomised test, which measures what the offer keeps directly

distractors.why_relevant: the retention model's calibration by risk band, which looks like the chance each list member cancels without the offer
distractors.why_unused: it describes the chance of cancelling within 30 days, not what the offer changes; the test's arms give that directly; no figure reads it
distractors.ruled_out_by: the test's holdout arm (the outcome without the offer, measured)

stated_inputs: half price on the next two monthly bills

sources.origin: constructed for this task by task177/generator/build.py (seeded, deterministic) around a fictional national news publisher in the United Kingdom (Daily Lantern Media, publisher of The Daily Lantern), its legacy billing system and its subscriptions platform. Subscribers are identified by number only. No real organisation's records or person is depicted.
